Q: How can a beginner convert a CMS-based store into a fully custom website? A:

What you’re describing isn’t really a “conversion” it’s effectively a full rebuild of your site without the CMS. For a beginner, that’s doable, but it’s important to approach it in stages rather than trying to replace everything at once.

A “fully custom website” can mean different things:

  • Custom frontend + existing backend (recommended for beginners)

  • Fully custom backend + frontend (much harder)

  • Headless CMS setup (middle ground)

If you’re new, the easiest path is:

  • Keep WordPress as a backend (or another CMS)

  • Build a custom frontend using something like React/Vue

This avoids rebuilding things like:

  • Authentication

  • Admin dashboards

  • Product management

Pick beginner-friendly tools:

Instead of building everything from scratch, use tools that reduce complexity:

  • Frontend frameworks: Next.js or Vue.js

  • Styling: plain CSS, Tailwind, or a component library

  • Ecommerce backends (if leaving WordPress):

    • Shopify (very beginner-friendly)

    • WooCommerce (if staying close to WordPress)

If you want minimal backend work, Shopify + a custom frontend is often the easiest transition.

If you change URLs without planning, you’ll lose rankings.

Make sure to:

  • Keep the same URL structure where possible

  • Add 301 redirects from old URLs to new ones

  • Preserve:

    • Page titles

    • Meta descriptions

    • Heading structure

Also resubmit your sitemap in Google Search Console after launch.

Q: Is there any way to reduce the size of my virtual env A:

You generally can’t shrink a virtual environment after the fact in a meaningful way, but you can reduce its size depending on how you create and manage it.

If you want to avoid duplicating large libraries like Django, you can create the virtualenv with access to system-wide packages:

python -m venv venv --system-site-packages

Downside = This only works if your hosting provider (e.g. PythonAnywhere) has the packages installed system-wide.

For the rest, i really don't know. I'd recommend removing unneeded packages.
